title: The four Deluxe sides and the poor disks
summary: He lists the issued titles, praises Billy Eckstine's songwriting and laments the bad pressings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: We did that, and we did another tune that Billy sang called "That's the Way You Feel," which is an original tune by Billy that Jerry did a beautiful arrangement on. Incidentally, Billy's writing talents are really something that... He's a hell of a songwriter, you know, as far as tunes are concerned. I don't know why he hasn't exploited it more than he has. And I hear sing now a lot of times, and I wonder why he doesn't do some of those old things that he wrote himself.
I said that we did six sides on that date, but I believe there were four that we did for Deluxe. There was "Opus X,"
"Blowing The Blues Away," "I'll Wait and Pray" and "If That's The Way You Feel" which Billy sang on -- and Sarah sang on "I'll Wait and Pray."

Anyway, the record date came out good, and all the guys played well. The only thing that was wrong was the fact that the records were just so bad, the disk was so bad, and the recording situation during those days was just bad. There's not very much left of those records now. It's really a shame, I think, because I really feel like they would bring out some of the things in the band that was happening in the beginning of it. There are a few records around of it, and there are records of these particular things that was later taken from air shots and things like that. But that particular date, you don't hear it very much because of these bad recording disks.
